messages:
elaine: Quick check — picking between per-call retry vs session-level retry budget for the compact session transport. Thoughts?

matt: I lean session-level for compact sessions. Keeps cursor semantics simpler and avoids retry storms when we do prefetch.

sanjeev: Session-level sounds good but need clear escape hatches. If a client wants per-request behavior we should expose a flag.

elaine: Agree. Main tradeoff: session budget lets us amortize tokens across pages, but complicates cancellation semantics.

fiona: Also we need to consider cross-lang ergonomics (py/ts/go). TS folks expect per-call opts often.

matt: Proposal sketch: default = session-budgeted retries (N total attempts across the session), opt-in per-call override via call-level header.

elaine: Can we show short examples for SDK ergonomics so API folks can review?

matt: TS example: ```ts
const sess = client.session({ retryBudget: 5 });
await sess.iteratePages({ pageSize: 50 });
// override on one call
sess.iteratePages({ pageSize: 10, retryBudget: 1 });
```

matt: Python example: ```py
s = Client.session(retry_budget=5)
for page in s.iter_pages(page_size=50):
    ...
# one-off override
s.iter_pages(page_size=10, retry_budget=1)
```

fiona: Go pattern: use functional opts; default session opts, WithRetryBudget(1) for per-call.

elaine: Cool. Implementation concerns: transport layer must maintain small state (remaining attempts) keyed by session id and decrement on each retried RPC. Also expose metrics: session.retry_budget_remaining.

sanjeev: We need to be careful with concurrency. Multiple inflight pages from same session could race to consume the budget. Two options: a) pessimistic lock per-session, b) optimistic CAS on in-memory counter. CAS preferred for perf.

matt: Agree CAS. We'll implement token-bucket-like int counter with atomic decrement. Document that budget is non-guaranteed across races (best-effort fairness).

elaine: What about pagination and resume tokens? If a retry consumes budget and the resumed call succeeds, do we charge the resumed attempt or refund?

sanjeev: Simpler: every outgoing RPC attempt consumes budget, no refunds. Trying to refund introduces complexity on partial receipts/duplicate tokens.

fiona: Sounds pragmatic. Call it out in docs and surface a telemetry tag so customers can detect when budgets were exhausted vs RPC errors.

matt: Also propose a very small default budget (2) to stop surprise costs. Enterprise could bump at session creation.

elaine: Backward compatibility: current clients expect stateless per-call retries. We need a migration plan: rollout behind a feature-flag and default to old behavior for 2 weeks, then flip for new minor-release with clear changelog.

ci-bot: Deploy pipeline note: feature-flag gate needs console + API toggle + telemetry. See https://devops.internal/features/CF-1234

elaine: Action items:
• matt: prototype atomic budget counter in runtime and a minimal session middleware (due EOD Fri).
• sanjeev: write concurrency note and tests for race scenarios (unit + stress).
• fiona: draft SDK examples & docs for py/ts/go and feature-flag wording.
• ela ine: schedule a 30m sync if prototype exposes edgecases.

matt: SGTM. Will post prototype thread with microbenchmark numbers.

sanjeev: Also adding one more check: ensure fallback to per-call semantics when session id absent (older clients).

elaine: Good catch. Decision for now: default session-budgeted retries when session id present, otherwise per-call retries. We'll capture this in the RFC follow-up doc. :white_check_mark:
